evidence.quote:
The tendency of the individual life is to be
static rather than dynamic, and this tendency is made into a
propulsion by civilization, where the obvious only is seen, and
the unexpected rarely happens.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator presents a general principle about the static tendency of individuals under civilization.

evidence.quote:
When the unexpected does
happen, however, and when it is of sufficiently grave import, the
unfit perish.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator explains a survival principle in which the unfit die when confronted by the unexpected.

evidence.quote:
The effect of civilization is to impose human law upon
environment until it becomes machine-like in its
regularity.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator explains that civilization makes the environment machine-like and regular.

evidence.quote:
The fall of
1897 found them at Dyea, but without the money to carry an outfit
across Chilcoot Pass and float it down to Dawson.
evidence.paraphrase: The characters relocate to the Alaskan frontier during the Klondike gold rush.

evidence.quote:
The old cabin was gone forever.
The horizon of life was
totally new and unfamiliar.
The unexpected had swept its
wizardry over the face of things, changing the perspective,
juggling values, and shuffling the real and the unreal into
perplexing confusion.
evidence.paraphrase: After the murders, the characters' world is described as wholly transformed and unfamiliar.

evidence.quote:
He was carrying a shot-gun.
Even as they looked, he lifted
it to his shoulder and fired twice.
evidence.paraphrase: Dennin suddenly shoots and kills two of the party at breakfast.

evidence.quote:
It was the unexpected.
Hans and Edith were
stunned.
They sat at the table with bodies tense, their
eyes fixed in a fascinated gaze upon the murderer.
evidence.paraphrase: Hans and Edith are stunned and paralyzed by the sudden killings.

evidence.quote:
she made original sociological researches and worked out for
herself the evolution of the law.
It came to her that the
law was nothing more than the judgment and the will of any group
of people.
evidence.paraphrase: Edith reasons out the nature and origin of law through her own step-by-step inquiry.

evidence.quote:
Why, then, could not one
thousand people constitute such a group? she asked herself.
And if one thousand, why not one hundred?
Why not
fifty?
Why not five?
Why not

two?
evidence.paraphrase: Edith applies successive reasoning to conclude that even two people can constitute a law-making group.

evidence.quote:
Between them they constituted the
majority of this particular group.
It was the group-will
that Dennin should be hanged.
In the execution of this will
Edith strove earnestly to observe the customary forms, but the
group was so small that Hans and she had to serve as witnesses,
as jury, and as judges
also as executioners.
evidence.paraphrase: Applying her reasoning about law, the couple conducts a full trial and execution by themselves.

evidence.quote:
death, instead of stalking about grewsome and
accidental, becomes a prearranged pageant, moving along a
well-oiled groove to the family vault
evidence.paraphrase: Death in civilization is contrasted as an orderly pageant versus its grim accidental nature.

evidence.quote:
But the Indians remained solemnly to watch the working of the
white man
s law that compelled a man to dance upon the
air.
evidence.paraphrase: The Indians observe the execution as a demonstration of white man's law.
